text:
Dougie Hamilton has 9 points in 17 games, and Pucks and Pitchforks wrote this month that he is playing like a first-line defenseman again. Our numbers agree with the spirit of that. New Jersey takes 60.4 percent of the expected goals with him on at 5v5, and the Devils have scored 6.6 fewer goals than those chances deserve. He is owed some points.

The shot volume is the Hamilton signature: 46 shots in 17 games, at 4.3 percent shooting, below the defenseman norm. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a less famous strength, that he stops 18 percent of the entries aimed at him against a typical 11, and Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile last season.

He set up Jesper Bratt's overtime winner against St. Louis with a defensive play and scored the 4-4 power-play goal against the Islanders on Saturday. Heavy reports he is about to pass a franchise legend in a key stat. At 33, playing 20 minutes a night, he looks like the right man in the right role.
headline: Hamilton's points haven't caught up to his play
